title: Large-scale PD disaggregation cascade when a prefill or decode server goes offline
body: I am deploying qwen3-32b-fp8 in PD disaggregation mode with 90 prefill servers and 30 decode servers on H20 GPUs. When a prefill server is restarted or migrated, affected decoder requests fail and the decode server continuously retries the unavailable prefill. Its health check then times out, sglang-router removes it, and high-QPS traffic is concentrated on the remaining decode servers until they crash. Decoder logs show disconnected health-check requests, 20-second detokenizer timeouts, and health-check failures. I am unsure whether the problem is invalid routing from the gateway or retry behavior inside the SGLang server.

symptoms_visible: When a prefill server is restarted or migrated, decode requests fail and the corresponding decode servers keep retrying until their health checks time out.
The router removes those decode workers, sends traffic to the few remaining workers, and under high QPS those workers crash within seconds.
The decoder log reports disconnected HEALTH_CHECK requests and says it could not get a response from the detokenizer for 20 seconds.
N0.label: N0 cascading PD failure reported

symptoms_visible: The cascading retry and health-check timeout occurs on SGLang 0.5.9.
N1.label: N1 deployed version established

symptoms_visible: With SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=1, the decoder still keeps retrying the unavailable prefill and its requests and health checks still time out.
N1_x.label: N1_x heartbeat threshold workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: In a three-prefill, one-decode reproduction with eight clients, killing one prefill makes the decoder repeatedly log connection refused for that prefill bootstrap port and retry up to 20 times.
N2.label: N2 minimal reproduction collected

symptoms_visible: After applying the first retry-reduction patch, continuously sending requests in the 3P1D test still leaves the decoder retrying the dead prefill for about one minute.
N2_x.label: N2_x retry-reduction patch aftermath

symptoms_visible: With the first drain-logic patch applied to the 3P1D setup, the prefill server becomes stuck as soon as it receives a request and later reports 300-second bootstrap timeouts.
N3_x.label: N3_x drain patch race aftermath

symptoms_visible: On main with the revised patch, the decode side continues serving requests after I kill a prefill and no longer blocks, although connection-refused retries still appear and the router does not remove the dead prefill immediately.
N4.label: N4 decode blocking mitigated

symptoms_visible: In my 2P2D nginx-based failure test with 16 clients, killing either the prefill or decode proxy makes a corresponding peer server stop processing requests for about a minute before it recovers.
During one observed gap from 15:01:49 to 15:02:39, only the metrics endpoint responded; after 20 seconds the server logged that it had received no detokenizer response.
N5.label: N5 reciprocal health-check failure isolated

symptoms_visible: With the candidate patch and router health checks set to a 1-second interval and 2-second timeout, killing one prefill or decode instance no longer affects the other decode or prefill instances.
N6.label: N6 candidate health-check fix verified

symptoms_visible: After applying the verified health-check correction, taking one prefill or decode instance offline no longer stalls or removes the otherwise healthy peer instances.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Are you running the main branch or a released version?
Which exact SGLang version is deployed?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am running the current main branch rather than 0.5.9, but the same failure occurs.

edges.comment: Messages c0-c1, describing the original reporter's deployment: participant1 asked whether the issue occurred on main or 0.5.9, and the reporter answered 0.5.9.

solution.intent: Set the disaggregation heartbeat maximum failure count to one so requests affected by a missing prefill are aborted quickly.
solution.concrete_example: Export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=1 before starting the PD servers, then repeat the prefill restart test.

edges.comment: Messages c2-c5 on the reporter's deployment: participant1 suggested the heartbeat threshold; the reporter tried it, said it did not work, and independently reported the 20-retry fetch loop and pending requests not clearing.

question_patterns: Can you provide a minimal setup and exact steps that reproduce the failure?
Please share the server, router, load-generator, and failure-injection commands.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it with three prefill servers, one decode server, the PD router, and eight client threads continuously sending long requests. After a while I kill -9 one prefill process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it in 3P1D; it only occurs in the 90P30D production deployment and no decoder retries appear in the small setup.
The same reproduction works with four clients instead of eight.

question_patterns: What does the decoder log print immediately after the prefill process is killed?
Please paste the raw connection and retry lines from the decoder.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The decoder logs connection refused for 127.0.0.1:8998 and prints 'Prefill server info not available from 127.0.0.1:8998, retrying (2/20)...'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The decoder immediately aborts the affected request and never retries the dead bootstrap address.

edges.comment: Message c6 from the original reporter: complete local 3P1D reproduction, eight-client load generator, kill command, and raw decoder retry output.

solution.intent: Apply the first proposed retry-reduction patch to reduce how long the decoder retries an unavailable prefill.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the first candidate patch that lowers the prefill-info retry count, then repeat the continuous 3P1D load and kill one prefill.

edges.comment: Messages c7-c9 on the reporter's 3P1D system: the reporter applied the first candidate patch and found that it only eased the retries; the decoder still retried for roughly one minute.

solution.intent: Replace the synchronous retry path with background drain and resolving logic so unavailable peers do not block request handling.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the candidate drain and resolving refactor, then rerun the 3P1D request test.
solution.inference_hint: After the reporter supplied the stuck-prefill log, the maintainer identified a race in the drain logic. That diagnosis is engineer-side rather than part of the reporter's raw observation.

edges.comment: Messages c20-c24 on the original reporter's 3P1D test system: the first drain-logic implementation was applied and the prefill stalled upon receipt of a request; participant1 acknowledged a race condition.

solution.intent: Revise the implementation so peer-resolution retries no longer block the request path while retaining a later opportunity to resolve peers that start late.
solution.concrete_example: Use the revised main-branch patch where retry logic no longer blocks request handling, then kill one prefill under load and inspect whether the decoder continues serving.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer explained that the revised implementation moved retry logic out of the blocking path. The reporter's evidence is that request service continued despite connection-refused logs.

edges.comment: Messages c25-c35 on the same reporter's deployment: after additional revisions, the reporter tested main plus the patch and confirmed that decode requests no longer blocked, while stale routing and repeated connection errors remained.

question_patterns: Does the analogous failure occur when a decode instance becomes unreachable, and what topology are you testing?
Can you reproduce the remaining issue in both directions and describe how you simulate the failed node?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested with 2P2D behind nginx and 16 clients. I simulate a node failure with pkill nginx, which makes that server unreachable for 60 seconds before our Kubernetes setup restarts it. Killing either the prefill or decode proxy makes a corresponding peer instance appear stalled for about a minute.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Killing a decode proxy has no effect on any prefill, and the remaining decode handles all retried requests normally.
The same reciprocal failure occurs in 2P3D rather than 2P2D.

question_patterns: How long does the corresponding peer stop processing traffic before it recovers?
What is the observable duration of the request-processing gap?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Virtually, the corresponding decode or prefill instance stalls for about a minute and then recovers.

question_patterns: Can you share timestamps showing what the affected server processes during the stall?
What endpoints, if any, continue responding during the gap?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found an empty processing window from 15:01:49 to 15:02:39. Only GET /metrics continued to return 200 during that period.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Chat completions continue returning 200 throughout the interval; only metrics logging pauses.

question_patterns: What health-check message appears during the processing gap?
Please paste the raw health-check timeout line with its timing.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At 15:02:10 the log says: 'Health check failed. Server couldn't get a response from detokenizer for last 20 seconds.' The last heartbeat shown is 15:01:49.

edges.comment: Messages c36-c41, all describing the original reporter's extended testing: the reporter tested the symmetric decode-loss case in a 2P2D nginx and Kubernetes setup and supplied the raw processing gap and health timeout.

question_patterns: Please test the candidate build, repeat the prefill and decode failure tests, and report whether healthy peer instances are still affected.
Can you test the candidate build in both failure directions and tell me what you observe?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Great, this patch seems to really work. Killing one prefill or decode instance no longer affects the other decode or prefill instances. I tested with the router health-check interval set to 1 second and timeout set to 2 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the candidate build, killing one peer still causes the other side to stop serving for about a minute.
The candidate works with a 2-second health-check interval instead of 1 second.

edges.comment: Messages c42-c46 on the original reporter's deployment: participant1 requested a pre-landing test and the reporter verified the candidate in both failure directions. This is a measurement and does not change the retained system state.

solution.intent: Ship the verified health-check correction so queued work involving an unavailable PD peer does not cause an otherwise functioning worker to be marked unhealthy and turn delayed router detection into a cascade.
solution.concrete_example: Use a build containing the verified health-check correction and prompt router health checks; when one prefill or decode disappears, fail or reroute affected work without allowing unrelated peer workers to be removed or stalled.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter's raw evidence shows requests reaching an unavailable peer, a long interval with no normal request processing, and a health failure after 20 seconds without detokenizer output. The maintainer's final diagnosis was that health-check logic incorrectly amplified those requests into worker removal; delayed router detection was a trigger, not a sufficient explanation for the cascade by itself.

edges.comment: Final accepted resolution from c40-c46: participant1 tied the series of failures to the health-check logic, supplied a correction, and the original reporter verified that killing either kind of PD instance no longer affected healthy peers. The fix is scored descriptively because the thread links the final patch without reproducing its implementation.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted diagnosis: delayed worker detection can send work toward a dead PD peer, but faulty server health-check behavior amplifies that event by marking otherwise functioning workers unhealthy after queued work produces no detokenizer response.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: reproducible connection-refused retries, the roughly one-minute processing gap where only metrics responded, and the 20-second no-detokenizer health-check error.
Must recommend isolating, rerouting, or fast-failing requests affected by a dead prefill or decode while keeping unrelated healthy workers available.
Must not present SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=1, merely reducing the retry count, or the first drain implementation as the fix; each was tried and did not resolve the case.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the health-check correction in both prefill-loss and decode-loss scenarios before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical production operator who can inspect scheduler code, build and cherry-pick candidate changes, run multi-node PD deployments, inject process and proxy failures, and analyze detailed server logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, evidence-driven, and cooperative; provides complete reproduction scripts and long raw logs, challenges explanations that conflict with observed timing, and prefers fast failure over user-visible timeouts.
